intro: Every German modal verb has an objective reading, which describes the world (obligation, permission, ability, someone else’s instruction, intention, liking), and most also have a subjective reading, in which the speaker says how sure they are: muss (certain), müsste / sollte (expected), dürfte (probable), kann / könnte (possible), kann nicht (ruled out), mag (conceded). Two modals report what others or the subject say: sollen (hearsay) and wollen (self-claim). The 21 sentences here cover all three readings. Most gaps take the modal itself, including the Konjunktiv II forms dürfte, könnte and müsste. Three take a perfect infinitive and have two gaps (muss … geregnet haben, soll … abgesagt haben, will … gewesen sein). The last five give you the synonymous phrase that formal prose uses instead of a modal: es ist erforderlich, es steht zu erwarten, es ist nicht auszuschließen, angeblich, vermutlich. The cue in brackets always names the reading, so read it before you choose.
tips[0].title: Objective: what the world requires, allows, enables
tips[0].text: müssen = es ist erforderlich · nicht brauchen zu = es ist nicht erforderlich · dürfen = es ist gestattet · können = imstande sein / es ist möglich · sollen = ein anderer verlangt es · wollen = beabsichtigen · mögen = gern haben. With a negation, können and dürfen can also judge whether something is justified: Das kann man ihm nicht vorwerfen (= the reproach would be unjustified). That is still an objective statement, not a guess.
tips[0].trap: nicht müssen means “not have to”; the prohibition is nicht dürfen. In careful written German nicht brauchen takes zu: Sie brauchen nicht zu kommen.
tips[0].check.why: Only brauchen takes zu here: nicht brauchen zu means 'not have to'. nicht dürfen would forbid it.
tips[1].title: Subjective: a scale of certainty
tips[1].text: muss (the speaker is sure) › müsste / sollte (it ought to be so, if all goes normally) › dürfte (probable) › kann / könnte (possible) › mag (conceded, “granted”). kann nicht rules something out. The subjective reading is signalled by a state verb (sein, haben, liegen) or, for the past, by the perfect infinitive: Partizip II + haben / sein.
tips[1].trap: Er muss arbeiten is an obligation; Er muss gearbeitet haben is an inference. For past guesses, keep the modal in the present and put the past into the infinitive: not *Er musste krank sein* but Er muss krank gewesen sein.
tips[1].check.why: A sure inference about the past keeps the modal in the present and puts the past into the infinitive: muss geregnet haben.
tips[2].title: Reporting: sollen for others, wollen for oneself
tips[2].text: Er soll … = people say he …: the speaker passes on a claim without vouching for it. Er will … = he himself claims …, and the speaker doubts it. Both take the perfect infinitive for past claims. Press and court reports depend on them.
tips[2].trap: Er will nichts gewusst haben does not mean “he wants to have known nothing”; it means “he claims to have known nothing”.
tips[2].check.why: wollen with a perfect infinitive reports the subject’s own claim, which the speaker doubts; soll would be what others say.
tips[3].title: Every reading has a phrase
tips[3].text: Formal writing often replaces the modal with a phrase, and a good writer moves between the two in both directions. muss (Pflicht) ↔ es ist erforderlich · muss (Gewissheit) ↔ zweifellos · dürfte ↔ vermutlich / es steht zu erwarten · kann, könnte ↔ es ist nicht auszuschließen · soll (Hörensagen) ↔ angeblich / Berichten zufolge · will ↔ er behauptet.
tips[3].check.why: es ist nicht auszuschließen expresses possibility, which is könnte; muss would be certainty and soll hearsay.
remember[0]: Objective (the world), subjective (the speaker’s certainty), reporting (the source): one modal, up to three readings.
remember[1]: Subjective past = modal in the present + perfect infinitive: muss geregnet haben, kann nicht eingeworfen haben.
remember[2]: soll = others say so; will = he says so himself.
remember[3]: Know the phrase for each reading: erforderlich, vermutlich, es steht zu erwarten, nicht auszuschließen, angeblich.
table.caption: The modal system
mistakes[0].why: The subjective past needs the full perfect infinitive: Partizip II + sein / haben.
mistakes[1].why: For a present guess about the past the modal stays in the present; the past goes into the infinitive.
mistakes[2].why: Probability is expressed by the Konjunktiv II dürfte; darf is permission.
mistakes[3].why: soll reports what others say; a claim made by the subject about himself takes wollen.
hook: One small modal verb can command, permit, guess, doubt or pass on a rumour; learn to hear which one it’s doing.
recall.known: From the modal lessons: muss, dürfte, soll and will in their many uses.
recall.today: The whole system on one page: objective, subjective and reporting.
